![A net diagram of a cuboid with labelled dimensions: 7 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm. Diagram is labelled "Not to scale".](assets/001-a-net-diagram-of-a-cuboid-with-labelled-dimensio.png)

The diagram shows the net of a cuboid.

(i) Find the volume of the cuboid.

......................................... cm<sup>3</sup> [2]

(ii) Show that the total surface area of the cuboid is 122 cm<sup>2</sup>.

[2]

(iii) Calculate the total length of the edges of the cuboid.

.......................................... cm [2]
parts.solution_md:
(i)

> **[exam-tip]**
> The volume, $V$, of a cuboid is
> 
> $V=\mathrm{length}\times\mathrm{height}\times\mathrm{width}$
> 
> This is **not** included on the list of formulas given in the exam paper.

Multiply the three given dimensions together

- It doesn't matter which ones you call 'length', 'breadth' or 'width'

$7\times3\times4$

**[M1]**

Use your calculator to work that out

**Final answer:** **84 cm**<sup>**3**</sup>

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For $7\times3\times4$ or equivalent.
> 
> **A1**: For 84. Earning this mark automatically earns the preceding 'M' mark as well.

(ii)

> **[exam-tip]**
> The area, $A$, of a rectangle is
> 
> $A=\mathrm{length}\times\mathrm{width}$
> 
> This is **not** included on the list of formulas given in the exam paper.

You can fill in a few more of the side lengths to help you see the sizes of the different faces

![Net of a cuboid with labelled dimensions: 7 cm length, 4 cm width, 3 cm height. The net consists of six rectangles. Labelled "Not to scale".  An extra 4, 7 and 3 have been added to the diagram to show that the cuboid's surface is made up of rectangles with dimensions 7 by 3, 7 by 4, and 4 by 3.](assets/002-net-of-a-cuboid-with-labelled-dimensions-7-cm-le.png)

A 7 by 3 rectangle has area

$7\times3=21$

**[M1]**

- A 7 by 4 rectangle has area

$7\times4=28$

- A 4 by 3 rectangle has area

$4\times3=12$

The cuboid has two of each type of face

- so the total area is

`table row cell 2 cross times 21 plus 2 cross times 28 plus 2 cross times 12 end cell equals cell 42 plus 56 plus 24 end cell row blank equals 122 end table`

**Final answer:** **122 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For $7\times3$, $7\times4$ or $4\times3$ or equivalent, seen or implied.
> 
> **A1**: For `2 cross times open parentheses 7 cross times 3 plus 7 cross times 4 plus 4 cross times 3 close parentheses` or equivalent, leading to 122.

(iii)

> **[exam-tip]**
> Do **not** just add up the lengths of all the lines in the diagram!
> 
> - When the net is assembled into a cuboid, some of those lines meet and become the same edge

A cuboid has 12 edges

- 4 corresponding to each dimension of the cuboid

So the total length of the edges is

$4\times7+4\times3+4\times4$

**[M1]**

$=28+12+16\,=56$

**Final answer:** **56 cm**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For $4\times7+4\times3+4\times4$ or equivalent.
> 
> **A1**: For 56. Earning this mark automatically earns the preceding 'M' mark as well.

parts.problem_md:
A sphere has a volume of 381 cm<sup>3</sup>.

Show that the radius of the sphere is 4.50 cm, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> The formula for the volume, $V$, of a sphere is given on the list of formulas in the exam paper:
> 
> $V=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$
> 
> - where $r$ is the radius

Here you know the volume, and you want to know the radius

Start by putting the given volume into the formula in place of $V$

$381=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$

Now you need to solve that for $r$

- First multiply by 3, to get rid of the fraction on the right-hand side

`table row cell 3 cross times 381 end cell equals cell 3 cross times 4 over 3 pi r cubed end cell row 1143 equals cell 4 pi r cubed end cell end table`

- Then divide both sides by $4π$, to get rid of the $4π$ on the right-hand side

$\frac{1143}{4π}=r^{3}$

**[M1]**

- You can use your calculator to work out the value of that

$r^{3}=90.957049...$

- To find the value of $r$, take the cube root of that

  - Use your calculator's memory, or the Ans key, to make sure you are taking the cube root of that exact value

`r equals cube root of 90.957049... end root equals 4.497233...`

Round to 3 significant figures

- The fourth significant figure is a '7'

  - which tells you to round the third significant figure '9' up to a 10
  - That means put a zero where the '9' is
  
    - and increase the '4' before it by 1

**Final answer:** **4.50 cm (3 s.f.)**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For $r^{3}=\frac{1143}{4π}$ or equivalent.
> 
> **A1**: For 4.497..., correctly rounded to 4.50.

A sphere has a volume of 381 cm^3^.

Show that the radius of the sphere is 4.50 cm, correct to 3 significant figures.

........................................ cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> The formula for the surface area, $A$, of a sphere is given on the list of formulas in the exam paper:
> 
> $A=4πr^{2}$
> 
> - where $r$ is the radius
> 
> Note that you can answer this part of the question even if you couldn't answer part (a), by using the value for the radius given in part (a).

If you answered part (a), you can use the exact value for the radius from there

- Otherwise just use 4.50 as given in part (a) of the question

`A equals 4 cross times pi cross times open parentheses 4.497233... close parentheses squared`

**[M1]**

Use your calculator to work that out

$A=254.156238...$

Round to a suitable degree of accuracy

- In general you should round to 3 significant figures, unless the question specifies otherwise
- The fourth significant figure is a '1'

  - which tells you not to change the third significant figure '4'

**Final answer:** **254 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** (3 s.f.)**

**[A1]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> If you used 4.50 for the radius, you would find
> 
> `A equals 4 cross times pi cross times open parentheses 4.50 close parentheses squared equals 254.469004...`
> 
> - To 3 significant figures, that would also round to 254

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For `A equals 4 cross times pi cross times open parentheses 4.497233... close parentheses squared` or $A=4\timesπ\times4.50^{2}$ or equivalent.
>
